paperTitle: O-Level English — Basic Band Practice 04: The Deep End
provenanceNote: NOT STUDENT-FACING. Basic band (2026-08-14). Original narrative written for the morning-quiz bank; NOT from any past exam paper. Spec: ~250-word passage, high-frequency vocabulary, short sentences, 5 questions / 5 marks, 3 of them click-only. Q1-Q2 short answer (1-4 words), Q3 vocabulary in context, Q4 literal, Q5 feeling — all MCQ.

sections.instruction: Read the story below and answer the questions that follow. [2 marks]. Write short answers. One or two words are enough.
sections.passage:
Paragraph 1
I can swim. I have been able to swim since I was nine. But I had never swum where my feet could not touch the floor.

Paragraph 2
At our school swimming test, we had to cross the pool at the deep end. Twenty-five metres. Nothing under you.

Paragraph 3
I stood at the edge for a long time. The others went in one by one. My turn came and I did not move.

Paragraph 4
Coach Lim did not shout. He sat down on the wet tiles beside my feet, which made him look shorter than me.

Paragraph 5
'Can you swim ten metres?' he asked.

Paragraph 6
'Yes.'

Paragraph 7
'Then swim ten. I will walk beside you on the side. When you reach ten, stop and tell me if you want the next ten.'

Paragraph 8
I swam ten metres. He walked beside me the whole way, holding a long pole. I did not want it, but I liked knowing it was there.

Paragraph 9
At ten metres I did not stop. I swam the whole twenty-five. When I climbed out my arms were shaking.

Paragraph 10
Coach Lim did not say 'well done'. He said, 'Same time next week?' and I said yes before I could think about it.

questions.stem: Q1. From Paragraph 2, how many metres did the students have to cross? [1]
Q2. From Paragraph 8, what did Coach Lim hold as he walked beside the writer? [1]

questions.stem: Q3. In Paragraph 1, the writer says his feet 'could not touch the floor'. What does this mean? [1]

options.text: The water was too cold for him.
The water was deeper than he was tall.
The floor of the pool was slippery.

questions.stem: Q4. What did Coach Lim ask the writer to do first? [1]

options.text: Hold on to the long pole.

questions.stem: Q5. Why does the writer say yes 'before I could think about it' in Paragraph 10? [1]

options.text: He did not hear the question properly.
He was afraid of the coach.
He was too tired to answer carefully.
He knew he would say no if he stopped to worry.
